workstream: C08 — paddle∥ball concurrency + adaptive two-pass detector schedule (HANDOFF_V3 §6 item 4)

built.concurrency: analyzeVideo.ts now runs the paddle detector (detect_paddle.py) and ball candidate generator (ball_candidates.py) subprocesses concurrently (preparePaddleDetections ∥ prepareBallCandidates). Tracking phases stay sequential — ball gating consumes the selected paddle track. Error isolation: each prep returns a status union (ready/env_missing/failed); a failure in one stage becomes that stage's honest 'unavailable' reason and never poisons the other.
built.twoPass: OFF-by-default --two-pass flag (plus --sparse-stride, default 3): pass 1 sparse scan over the detect span; planTwoPassSchedule (paddleSchedule.ts, pure/unit-testable) plans stride-1 dense regions around event peaks, primary-track uncertainty (low-confidence obs + birth/death inside span), high paddle-speed change, and coverage holes; pass 2 runs the detector per dense region; passes merge into paddle-dets.json (dense copy wins grid-slot collisions). Provenance: paddle-schedule.json records the schedule, realized frame counts, and per-frame pass assignment (framesByPass); report.paddleSchedule carries the schedule. Two-pass mode never reuses a cached paddle-dets.json (a stride-1 artifact must not stand in for a scheduled one).
built.designNote: Uncertainty/missing-frame anchors come from the PRIMARY (densest) sparse candidate only: with all candidate tracks, background/crowd tracks' permanently-noisy confidences densified the entire span (measured on wm-volley-02: dense region = whole span, 74 frames processed vs 55 full-dense).

concurrencyByteIdentity.method: Exact detector/candidate commands analyzeVideo issues, run sequentially then concurrently, on 2 committed dev bundle clips (CPU, D-FINE dfine-medium-coco). Full-file byte compare, then compare with the wall-clock 'timing' block stripped.
concurrencyByteIdentity.honestCaveat: Full files are NOT byte-identical because the artifacts embed wall-clock timing (modelLoadSec/inferenceSecTotal/wallSecTotal/msPerFrame). Control: two SEQUENTIAL runs of the same command also differ only in those timing fields (verified on afn-sasebo-rally1 paddle). Everything except the timing block — all frames, boxes, scores, labels, window, detector metadata — is byte-identical sequential vs concurrent.

twoPassDemo.method: Same flow as preparePaddleDetections driven directly (pose is macOS-only): sparse stride-3 pass → buildPaddleTracks → planTwoPassSchedule with event peak = committed annotation contactMs (dev cases only) → stride-1 dense regions → merge. Baseline = full stride-1 scan of the same detect span.

afn-sasebo-rally1.honestNegative: two-pass processed MORE frames than full dense (54 vs 45): the span is only 1500ms and the 900ms event-peak pad plus an uncertainty region cover most of it, so sparse+dense overlap costs more than it saves. Savings scale with detect-span length relative to the dense pads; short event-gated spans should stay one-pass.

measurements.unitTests: packages/swing-lab: 12 test files, 159 passed / 4 skipped, including new test/paddleSchedule.test.ts (12 tests: no-dense-when-clean, event-peak pad, span clamping, birth/death + low-confidence uncertainty, speed-change, missing-frames holes, region merge + reason union, fewer-than-full-scan, dense-wins merge collisions, timing accumulation, per-frame pass provenance). pnpm --filter @pickle/swing-lab typecheck passes.

environmentNotes.ffmpegStride: System ffmpeg 4.4.2 (Ubuntu 22.04) lacks -fps_mode (added in 5.1), so detect_paddle.py --stride N decodes 0 frames on stock Linux. Demos above used a static ffmpeg 7.0.2 on PATH. The repo tool was NOT modified.
environmentNotes.venv: tools/paddle-lab/.venv built with python3.10 (3.12 unavailable here) + torch 2.13.0+cpu, torchvision 0.28.0+cpu, transformers 5.16.1.
